definition: A training schedule technique that gradually increases the learning rate from a small value at the start of training before transitioning to the main schedule.
details: Learning rate warmup helps stabilize training in the early stages, particularly for large transformer models, where using the full target learning rate immediately can lead to instability or divergence.
story: Imagine teaching a friend to shoot a basketball. They miss, and you walk them backwards through the shot — elbow, wrist, release — to find what needs fixing. It is the same loop you use to learn anything: try, miss, correct, try again. Underneath all the magic is a patient process of small improvements. It is learning from every miss instead of repeating the same mistake. And that is Warmup (learning rate) — the quiet loop that turns flailing into skill.
